analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Acute bronchiolitis is a common and clinically heterogeneous lower respiratory tract infection in infancy, and while current guidelines discourage routine bronchodilator use, physiological responsiveness may exist in some patients. Tidal breathing analysis (TBA) offers a non-invasive, bedside method to objectively assess respiratory mechanics and quantify physiological changes after bronchodilator administration.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This case study reports on a 23-month-old boy with severe RSV bronchiolitis-like wheezing illness complicated by acute respiratory failure, in whom bronchodilator responsiveness was evaluated using predefined TBA parameters before and after inhaled bronchodilator administration.
analysis_en.methods: Bronchodilator responsiveness was assessed using tidal breathing analysis (TBA) to measure predefined parameters including time to peak tidal expiratory flow (tPTEF), tPTEF/TE ratio, expiratory time (TE), total respiratory cycle duration (Ttot), tidal volume (VT), minute ventilation (MV), and peak expiratory flow before and after bronchodilator administration.
analysis_en.main_results: Following treatment, tPTEF increased from 0.17 to 0.33 s (+94%), and the tPTEF/TE ratio increased from 0.12 to 0.27 (+125%). TE and Ttot decreased by 12.6% and 5.1%, respectively, while VT and MV increased by 12.1% and 18.3%. Peak expiratory flow remained unchanged at 0.14 L/s.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: This is among the first reports using bedside TBA to characterize acute bronchodilator responsiveness in severe bronchiolitis-like illness, with improvements in expiratory timing indices consistent with improved expiratory flow dynamics, supporting the hypothesis of a bronchodilator-responsive physiological phenotype.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that TBA-defined bronchodilator responsiveness may represent an early physiological marker in severe bronchiolitis, potentially supporting individualized treatment strategies and informing future longitudinal studies on its predictive value for recurrent wheezing or asthma.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: This is a single case study, limiting generalizability and statistical power, but the objective measurements and clear physiological changes provide moderate evidence for the feasibility of TBA in assessing bronchodilator responsiveness in severe bronchiolitis.

papers.title_zh: 潮式呼吸分析为客观评估急性呼吸力学和支气管扩张剂反应性提供了一种非侵入性床旁方法 毛细支气管炎
papers.source_body_en: Background: Acute bronchiolitis is among the most common causes of lower respiratory tract infection in infancy and remains a clinically heterogeneous syndrome. Current international guidelines recommend supportive management and generally discourage routine bronchodilator administration; however, physiological responsiveness may exist in a subset of patients. Tidal breathing analysis (TBA) provides a non-invasive, bedside method for objectively assessing respiratory mechanics and may objectively quantify physiological changes following bronchodilator administration. Case Presentation We report a 23-month-old boy presenting with severe RSV bronchiolitis-like wheezing illness complicated by acute respiratory failure. Bronchodilator responsiveness was evaluated using predefined TBA parameters before and after inhaled bronchodilator administration. Following treatment, time to peak tidal expiratory flow (tPTEF) increased from 0.17 to 0.33 s (+94%), while the tPTEF/TE ratio increased from 0.12 to 0.27 (+125%). Expiratory time (TE) and total respiratory cycle duration (Ttot) decreased by 12.6% and 5.1%, respectively, whereas tidal volume (VT) and minute ventilation (MV) increased by 12.1% and 18.3%. Peak expiratory flow remained unchanged (0.14 L/s before and after bronchodilator administration). Discussion To our knowledge, this is among the first reports using bedside TBA to characterize acute bronchodilator responsiveness in severe bronchiolitis-like illness. The improvement in expiratory timing indices, accompanied by shorter expiratory time without changes in peak expiratory flow, is consistent with improved expiratory flow dynamics following bronchodilator administration. These findings support the hypothesis that a bronchodilator-responsive physiological phenotype may exist. Previous studies have demonstrated an association between severe bronchiolitis during infancy and subsequent recurrent wheezing or asthma; however, whether acute bronchodilator responsiveness, measured objectively by TBA, represents a testable hypothesis for future longitudinal studies. Conclusions This case illustrates the feasibility of bedside TBA for identifying physiological bronchodilator responsiveness in severe bronchiolitis-like illness. Prospective longitudinal studies are warranted to determine whether TBA-defined responsiveness represents an early physiological marker requiring prospective validation and whether such physiological stratification may support individualized follow-up strategies.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:急性 毛细支气管炎 是婴儿下呼吸道感染的最常见原因之一,并且仍然是一种临床异质综合征。目前的国际指南建议支持性治疗,通常不鼓励常规使用支气管扩张剂;然而,部分患者可能存在生理反应。潮式呼吸分析 (TBA) 提供了一种非侵入性床旁方法,用于客观评估呼吸力学,并可以客观量化支气管扩张剂给药后的生理变化。病例介绍 我们报告一名 23 个月大的男孩,患有严重的 RSV 毛细支气管炎 样喘息疾病,并发急性呼吸衰竭。在吸入支气管扩张剂给药之前和之后使用预定义的 TBA 参数评估支气管扩张剂反应性。治疗 后,潮气呼气流量峰值时间 (tPTEF) 从 0.17 秒增加至 0.33 秒 (+94%),而 tPTEF/TE 比率从 0.12 增加至 0.27 (+125%)。呼气时间 (TE) 和总呼吸周期持续时间 (Ttot) 分别减少 12.6% 和 5.1%,而潮气量 (VT) 和每分钟通气量 (MV) 增加 12.1% 和 18.3%。呼气峰流量保持不变(支气管扩张剂给药前后均为 0.14 L/s)。讨论 据我们所知,这是使用床边 TBA 来表征严重 毛细支气管炎 样疾病的急性支气管扩张剂反应性的首批报告之一。呼气正时指数的改善,伴随着呼气时间的缩短而呼气峰流量没有变化,与支气管扩张剂给药后呼气流量动力学的改善一致。这些发现支持了可能存在支气管扩张剂反应性生理表型的假设。先前的研究已证明婴儿期严重的 毛细支气管炎 与随后的复发性喘息或哮喘之间存在关联;然而,通过 TBA 客观测量的急性支气管扩张反应是否代表了未来纵向研究的可检验假设。结论 该病例说明了床边 TBA 确定严重 毛细支气管炎 样疾病中生理性支气管扩张剂反应性的可行性。有必要进行前瞻性纵向研究,以确定 TBA 定义的反应性是否代表需要前瞻性验证的早期生理标志,以及这种生理分层是否可以支持个体化的随访策略。

papers.title: Prevalence and genetic diversity of respiratory syncytial viruses circulating in Bulgaria, 2023-2025
papers.abstract: Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of acute respiratory infections (ARIs) with a considerable disease burden among children under 5 years of age. This study aimed to characterize the prevalence of RSV, genetic diversity of circulating strains, and amino acid variability in viral proteins, as well as identify mutations within the binding sites of monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) approved for RSV prophylaxis. Methods Nasopharyngeal specimens from 5,170 patients of all ages with ARI were tested for 13 respiratory viruses using multiplex real-time PCR. Representative RSV-positive samples were subjected to whole-genome sequencing, followed by phylogenetic and amino acid sequence analyses. Results RSV was positive in 303 (5.9%) patients, of whom 61 (20.1%) had co-infections with other respiratory viruses. Among children under 5 years of age, RSV was the most frequently detected pathogen in cases of bronchiolitis (30.6%) and pneumonia (12.6%). RSV-positive samples from the 2024-2025 season were genotyped, and predominance of RSV-A over RSV-B was observed. Phylogenetic analysis identified eight and seven genetic lineages within RSV-A and RSV-B, respectively, with A.D.1.11 and B.D.1.1 being the most prevalent. No substitutions were detected in the F protein antigenic sites of RSV-A (Ø, I-V), including the binding sites for nirsevimab (site Ø), palivizumab (site II), and clesrovimab (site IV). Conversely, RSV-B strains exhibited substitutions in antigenic sites Ø (n=3), I (n=2), and V (n=2). Conclusions RSV is a leading cause of severe respiratory disease in early childhood and demonstrates substantial genetic diversity among circulating strains. The absence of resistance-associated substitutions in the F protein indicates that currently circulating RSV strains remain susceptible to approved mAbs.
papers.journal: Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology

source_records.abstract: Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of acute respiratory infections (ARIs) with a considerable disease burden among children under 5 years of age. This study aimed to characterize the prevalence of RSV, genetic diversity of circulating strains, and amino acid variability in viral proteins, as well as identify mutations within the binding sites of monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) approved for RSV prophylaxis. Methods Nasopharyngeal specimens from 5,170 patients of all ages with ARI were tested for 13 respiratory viruses using multiplex real-time PCR. Representative RSV-positive samples were subjected to whole-genome sequencing, followed by phylogenetic and amino acid sequence analyses. Results RSV was positive in 303 (5.9%) patients, of whom 61 (20.1%) had co-infections with other respiratory viruses. Among children under 5 years of age, RSV was the most frequently detected pathogen in cases of bronchiolitis (30.6%) and pneumonia (12.6%). RSV-positive samples from the 2024-2025 season were genotyped, and predominance of RSV-A over RSV-B was observed. Phylogenetic analysis identified eight and seven genetic lineages within RSV-A and RSV-B, respectively, with A.D.1.11 and B.D.1.1 being the most prevalent. No substitutions were detected in the F protein antigenic sites of RSV-A (Ø, I-V), including the binding sites for nirsevimab (site Ø), palivizumab (site II), and clesrovimab (site IV). Conversely, RSV-B strains exhibited substitutions in antigenic sites Ø (n=3), I (n=2), and V (n=2). Conclusions RSV is a leading cause of severe respiratory disease in early childhood and demonstrates substantial genetic diversity among circulating strains. The absence of resistance-associated substitutions in the F protein indicates that currently circulating RSV strains remain susceptible to approved mAbs.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of acute respiratory infections (ARIs) with a considerable disease burden among children under 5 years of age.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study aimed to characterize the prevalence of RSV, genetic diversity of circulating strains, and amino acid variability in viral proteins, as well as identify mutations within the binding sites of monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) approved for RSV prophylaxis.
analysis.methods: Nasopharyngeal specimens from 5,170 patients of all ages with ARI were tested for 13 respiratory viruses using multiplex real-time PCR. Representative RSV-positive samples were subjected to whole-genome sequencing, followed by phylogenetic and amino acid sequence analyses.
analysis.main_results: RSV was positive in 303 (5.9%) patients, of whom 61 (20.1%) had co-infections with other respiratory viruses. Among children under 5 years of age, RSV was the most frequently detected pathogen in cases of bronchiolitis (30.6%) and pneumonia (12.6%).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The absence of resistance-associated substitutions in the F protein indicates that currently circulating RSV strains remain susceptible to approved mAbs.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings provide important insights into the genetic diversity of RSV strains and their susceptibility to monoclonal antibodies, which can inform surveillance, diagnosis, and the development of targeted interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to data from the 2024-2025 season and does not account for long-term trends or seasonal variations. The evidence is strong as it is based on direct testing and sequencing of RSV-positive samples.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the prevalence and genetic diversity of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in Bulgaria from 2023 to 2025. RSV was detected in 5.9% of patients with acute respiratory infections (ARIs), with a notable proportion of co-infections. Among children under 5, RSV was the most frequently identified pathogen in bronchiolitis and pneumonia cases. Whole-genome sequencing revealed substantial genetic diversity, with eight and seven lineages identified in RSV-A and RSV-B, respectively. The most prevalent lineages were A.D.1.11 and B.D.1.1. No resistance-associated substitutions were found in the F protein antigenic sites of RSV-A, suggesting susceptibility to approved monoclonal antibodies. In contrast, RSV-B strains showed substitutions in multiple antigenic sites. The study highlights the importance of monitoring RSV genetic variation for effective surveillance and treatment strategies. The evidence is strong, but the findings are limited to a single season, reducing generalizability.

papers.title: Genomic Evolution and Minority Variant Dynamics of RSV during the First Season of Nirsevimab Implementation in Italy (2024-2025)
papers.abstract: Abstract Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a leading cause of hospitalization despite the recent implementation of infant immunoprophylaxis programs. The inter- and intra-host level of genetic variation across the genome has not been extensively investigated. Hence, the aim of this study was to characterize the whole genome of RSV strains circulating within two Italian areas during the 2024-2025 RSV season, corresponding to the first season after implementation of the national nirsevimab prophylaxis program. Whole genome sequencing (WGS) was performed on 88 respiratory samples that tested positive for RSV. Clinical records showed that none of the sequenced patients had received nirsevimab prophylaxis. The WGS strains obtained in the present study were correlated with the RSV strains circulating in Europe using phylogenetic inference. A newly designed bioinformatic pipeline was developed to evaluate the extent of genetic variation within hosts and reveal the distribution of minority mutations among RSV lineages. RSV-A (n=54) showed significantly higher levels of nucleotide diversity than RSV-B (n=34). Among the RSV-A strains, lineage A.D.3 was the most prevalent (35/54, 64%), followed by A.D.1 (18/54, 33%). The A.D.5 lineage was identified in only one strain, while all 34 RSV-B strains were found to be lineage B.D.E. Analysis of variants across the major lineages (A.D.1, A.D.3 and B.D.E) revealed heterogeneous mutation patterns. The G, L and F genes showed the highest variability. Minority viral variants (0.02-0.05 frequency) followed the same gene-specific dynamics as the broader quasispecies population. A>G transitions consistent with ADAR activity were detected in all samples but their frequency was similar to the other nucleotide substitutions across the genomes. The analysis of minor variants also targeted mutations known to reduce nirsevimab efficacy, and none were detected. Overall, RSV-A showed substantially greater intra-genotypic and intra-host diversity than RSV-B. The elevated diversity in RSV-A resulted from a wider distribution of mutations across the viral genome, including both high-frequency substitutions that shaped the consensus sequence and low-frequency variants contributing to the underlying quasispecies complexity. Although no nirsevimab-treated patients were included in this study, the observed intra-host diversity highlights the importance of continued genomic surveillance to detect potential escape variants as prophylactic programs expand.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在描述 2024-2025 年 RSV 季节期间在意大利两个地区流行的 RSV 菌株的整个 基因组 的特征,这是实施国家 尼塞韦单抗 预防计划后的第一个,因为对 宿主 之间和内部水平的遗传变异的调查有限。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对来自未接受 基因组 预防的患者的 88 份呼吸道样本进行了完整的 基因组 测序,这些样本的 RSV 检测呈阳性。
elements_zh.methods: 开发了一种新设计的生物信息学管道,用于评估 宿主 内的遗传变异,并揭示 RSV 谱系中少数 突变 的分布,并通过系统发育推断将菌株与欧洲循环相关联。
elements_zh.main_results: RSV-A (n=54) 显示出显着高于 RSV-B (n=34) 的核苷酸多样性,其中 A.D.3 是最常见的 RSV-A 谱系 (64%),而所有 RSV-B 株均为 B.D.E.;G、L和F基因表现出最高的变异性,并且没有检测到已知会降低尼塞韦单抗功效的突变。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: RSV-A 多样性的增加是由于 突变 在 基因组 中分布更广泛,包括高频和低频变体,这突显了随着预防计划的扩大,持续使用 基因组监测 来检测潜在逃逸变体的重要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现为 尼塞韦单抗 实施下 RSV 进化 的 监测 策略提供了信息,强调需要监测可能影响预防效果的少数变异。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于缺乏接受 尼塞韦单抗 治疗的患者,限制了对逃逸变异的直接评估,但由于强大的测序和生物信息学分析,该研究为 RSV 基因组多样性和少数变异动态提供了高可信度的证据。

papers.title: Comparison of the Clinical Course of Viral Respiratory Infections in Hospitalized Patients During the 2025/2026 Season in Poland
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: SARS-CoV-2, influenza viruses, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remain major causes of adult hospitalizations, but contemporary comparative data are limited. This study compared the epidemiological characteristics, clinical presentation, and outcomes of adults hospitalized with these infections during the 2025/2026 epidemic season in Poland. Methods: We conducted a retrospective multicenter study of consecutive adults hospitalized with laboratory-confirmed COVID-19, influenza, or RSV infection between September 2025 and April 2026. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, vaccination status, clinical features, laboratory findings, and outcomes were analyzed. Independent predictors of in-hospital mortality were identified using multivariable logistic regression. Results: The study included 604 patients: 255 with COVID-19, 314 with influenza, and 35 with RSV infection. Distinct seasonal patterns were observed, with COVID-19 peaking in autumn, influenza in winter, and RSV in early spring. Most hospitalized patients were elderly and unvaccinated. RSV patients were older, more frequently affected by multimorbidity, ischemic heart disease, and cancer, and showed the greatest respiratory impairment, including the highest rates of hypoxemia and pneumonia. Influenza was characterized by more frequent fever, headache, and myalgia. Despite lower pneumonia rates, COVID-19 was associated with the highest in-hospital mortality (13.7%) and remained an independent predictor of death (aOR = 3.23, 95%CI: 1.68–6.22). Antibiotic use was common across all cohorts (62–77%). Conclusions: COVID-19 remained associated with the highest mortality among hospitalized adults, whereas RSV contributed substantially to respiratory morbidity in older individuals. These findings support improved vaccination uptake, continued surveillance, hospital preparedness, and antimicrobial stewardship.

papers.title: Dynamic regulation-based stabilizing mutations are highly effective for designing RSV pre-fusion F mRNA vaccines
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of respiratory tract infections and poses a serious threat to young children, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. We previously designed a pre-fusion stabilized F protein (pre-F), TriM-5, using a dynamic regulation mechanism, and produced a recombinant protein-based vaccine candidate that exhibited potent protection against RSV. However, several studies have revealed that the stabilization of pre-F achieved in protein form may not be sufficient for application in mRNA vaccine development. Here, based on TriM-5, we designed an mRNA vaccine candidate to assess whether the dynamic regulation-based stabilizing mutations of TriM-5 are also effective in an mRNA format. The TriM-5 mRNA was codon-optimized using in-house software named NVSI_GAmRNAopt, which employed a genetic algorithm incorporating multiple empirical parameters for coding sequence (CDS) optimization, and encapsulated using lipid nanoparticles (LNPs). Mouse immunization showed that after CDS optimization, the IgG antibody titers increased approximately threefold, indicating the effectiveness of our codon-optimization algorithm. Compared with the Moderna RSV mRNA sequence encapsulated with our proprietary BM028 LNPs, the TriM-5 mRNA-LNP induced 3.03-fold higher neutralizing antibody titers against RSV A2 virus, along with significantly higher IFN-γ, IL-5 and IL-17A secretion levels, indicating its superior immunogenicity. Virus challenge experiments demonstrated that both TriM-5 mRNA-LNP and Moderna mRNA-LNP reduced lung viral loads effectively, with no obvious lung pathology. The designed TriM-5 mRNA-LNP exhibits good immunogenicity and protective efficacy, and thereby may serve as a promising candidate for further vaccine development.

papers.title_zh: 基于动态调节的稳定 突变 对于设计 RSV 融合前 F mRNA 疫苗 非常有效
papers.source_body_en: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of respiratory tract infections and poses a serious threat to young children, older adults, and immunocompromised individuals. We previously designed a pre-fusion stabilized F protein (pre-F), TriM-5, using a dynamic regulation mechanism, and produced a recombinant protein-based vaccine candidate that exhibited potent protection against RSV. However, several studies have revealed that the stabilization of pre-F achieved in protein form may not be sufficient for application in mRNA vaccine development. Here, based on TriM-5, we designed an mRNA vaccine candidate to assess whether the dynamic regulation-based stabilizing mutations of TriM-5 are also effective in an mRNA format. The TriM-5 mRNA was codon-optimized using in-house software named NVSI_GAmRNAopt, which employed a genetic algorithm incorporating multiple empirical parameters for coding sequence (CDS) optimization, and encapsulated using lipid nanoparticles (LNPs). Mouse immunization showed that after CDS optimization, the IgG antibody titers increased approximately threefold, indicating the effectiveness of our codon-optimization algorithm. Compared with the Moderna RSV mRNA sequence encapsulated with our proprietary BM028 LNPs, the TriM-5 mRNA-LNP induced 3.03-fold higher neutralizing antibody titers against RSV A2 virus, along with significantly higher IFN-γ, IL-5 and IL-17A secretion levels, indicating its superior immunogenicity. Virus challenge experiments demonstrated that both TriM-5 mRNA-LNP and Moderna mRNA-LNP reduced lung viral loads effectively, with no obvious lung pathology. The designed TriM-5 mRNA-LNP exhibits good immunogenicity and protective efficacy, and thereby may serve as a promising candidate for further vaccine development.

papers.title: Defining the Role of the RSV Small Hydrophobic Protein in Viral Pathogenesis 2255472
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) accounts for 33 million infections worldwide each year and is the leading cause of lower respiratory tract infections in infants. Severe RSV-induced disease is associated with the host response to the infection including the increased production of the inflammatory cytokines IL-1β and IL-6. The RSV small hydrophobic (SH) protein has been previously implicated in regulating the secretion of IL-1β following infection. The SH protein is classified as a viroporin, a class of transmembrane proteins that oligomerize to form pores in membranes and can facilitate ion flux to modulate multiple signaling pathways. It is currently unknown what role SH may play in modulating RSV disease severity beyond the modulation of IL-1β production; however, in 2017 there was an outbreak of RSV-B cases containing a mutation in the SH protein that resulted in high hospitalization rates. This outbreak occurred in the summer, an unusual season for RSV cases prior to the COVID-19 pandemic, with the virus expressing a single nucleotide polymorphism within the SH protein that changed an asparagine into an aspartic acid at amino acid 64 (SH N64D). Methods To study the impact of the N64 mutation, we generated a recombinant A2 laboratory strain virus encoded with an aspartic acid at amino acid 63 which is termed A2 SH N63D. We utilized plaque assays, ELISAs, qPCR for cytosolic mtDNA, and human monocyte THP-1 cell lines with a dual reporter for NF-κB and type I IFN response. Results The A2 SH N63D mutant elicited decreased viral titers and early disease compared to the wildtype A2 (WT A2) in mice. We have also observed increased inflammatory cytokines and a type I IFN response following A2 SH N63D infection. We have observed mtDNA release after A2 SH N63D infection within THP-1 cells as well as a STING-dependent type I IFN response Conclusion These results suggest that the aspartic acid within the C-terminus of the SH protein may contribute to RSV pathogenesis and the type I IFN response. Funding Source NIAID R01 AI167249 Topic Categories Viral Immunology (VIR)

analysis.research_question_and_background: Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) accounts for 33 million infections worldwide each year and is the leading cause of lower respiratory tract infections in infants. The RSV small hydrophobic (SH) protein has been previously implicated in regulating the secretion of IL-1β following infection, but its role in modulating RSV disease severity beyond IL-1β production remains unknown.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study utilized a recombinant A2 laboratory strain virus encoded with an aspartic acid at amino acid 63 (A2 SH N63D) to investigate the impact of the N64 mutation. Experiments were conducted in mice and human monocyte THP-1 cell lines with a dual reporter for NF-κB and type I IFN response.
analysis.methods: Plaque assays, ELISAs, qPCR for cytosolic mtDNA, and human monocyte THP-1 cell lines with a dual reporter for NF-κB and type I IFN response were used to study the impact of the N64 mutation. The A2 SH N63D mutant was generated and compared to the wildtype A2 (WT A2).
analysis.main_results: The A2 SH N63D mutant elicited decreased viral titers and early disease compared to the wildtype A2 in mice. Increased inflammatory cytokines and a type I IFN response were observed following A2 SH N63D infection, along with mtDNA release within THP-1 cells and a STING-dependent type I IFN response.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results suggest that the aspartic acid within the C-terminus of the SH protein may contribute to RSV pathogenesis and the type I IFN response. This finding is novel as it expands the understanding of the SH protein's role beyond IL-1β modulation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings may inform the development of targeted therapies against RSV by focusing on the SH protein's role in pathogenesis. Understanding the SH protein's impact on disease severity could lead to improved surveillance and intervention strategies for RSV infections.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in mice and THP-1 cell lines, which may not fully recapitulate human RSV infection. The evidence strength is moderate due to the limited scope of the study and the use of laboratory strains rather than clinical isolates.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the role of the RSV small hydrophobic (SH) protein in viral pathogenesis, focusing on a specific mutation (N64D) observed in a 2017 outbreak. The researchers generated a recombinant A2 SH N63D mutant and compared it to wildtype A2 in mice and THP-1 cells. The mutant showed decreased viral titers and early disease in mice, along with increased inflammatory cytokines and a type I IFN response. The findings suggest that the aspartic acid in the SH protein's C-terminus contributes to RSV pathogenesis and the type I IFN response, potentially informing targeted therapies and surveillance strategies.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究利用第 63 位氨基酸编码天冬氨酸的重组 A2 实验室毒株病毒 (A2 SH N63D) 来研究 N64 突变 的影响。实验在小鼠和人单核细胞 THP-1 细胞系中进行,具有 NF-κB 和 I 型 IFN 反应的双报告基因。
elements_zh.methods: 使用噬菌斑测定、ELISA、胞质 mtDNA 的 qPCR 以及具有 NF-κB 和 I 型 IFN 反应双报告基因的人单核细胞 THP-1 细胞系来研究 N64 突变 的影响。生成 A2 SH N63D 突变体并与野生型 A2 (WT A2) 进行比较。
elements_zh.main_results: 与野生型 A2 相比,A2 SH N63D 突变体在小鼠体内引起病毒滴度降低和早期疾病。A2 SH N63D 感染后观察到炎症细胞因子增加和 I 型 IFN 反应,以及 THP-1 细胞内 mtDNA 释放和 STING 依赖性 I 型 IFN 反应。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 结果表明,SH 蛋白 C 末端的天冬氨酸可能有助于 RSV 发病机制 和 I 型 IFN 反应。这一发现很新颖,因为它扩展了对 SH 蛋白在 IL-1β 调节之外的作用的理解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 通过关注 SH 蛋白在 发病机制 中的作用,这些发现可能为针对 RSV 的靶向疗法的开发提供信息。了解 SH 蛋白对疾病严重程度的影响可能会改进 监测 和 RSV 感染的干预策略。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在小鼠和 THP-1 细胞系中进行的,这可能无法完全重现人类 RSV 感染。由于研究范围有限且使用实验室菌株而非临床分离株,证据强度中等。

papers.source_body_en: Abstract Introduction Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) accounts for 33 million infections worldwide each year and is the leading cause of lower respiratory tract infections in infants. Severe RSV-induced disease is associated with the host response to the infection including the increased production of the inflammatory cytokines IL-1β and IL-6. The RSV small hydrophobic (SH) protein has been previously implicated in regulating the secretion of IL-1β following infection. The SH protein is classified as a viroporin, a class of transmembrane proteins that oligomerize to form pores in membranes and can facilitate ion flux to modulate multiple signaling pathways. It is currently unknown what role SH may play in modulating RSV disease severity beyond the modulation of IL-1β production; however, in 2017 there was an outbreak of RSV-B cases containing a mutation in the SH protein that resulted in high hospitalization rates. This outbreak occurred in the summer, an unusual season for RSV cases prior to the COVID-19 pandemic, with the virus expressing a single nucleotide polymorphism within the SH protein that changed an asparagine into an aspartic acid at amino acid 64 (SH N64D). Methods To study the impact of the N64 mutation, we generated a recombinant A2 laboratory strain virus encoded with an aspartic acid at amino acid 63 which is termed A2 SH N63D. We utilized plaque assays, ELISAs, qPCR for cytosolic mtDNA, and human monocyte THP-1 cell lines with a dual reporter for NF-κB and type I IFN response. Results The A2 SH N63D mutant elicited decreased viral titers and early disease compared to the wildtype A2 (WT A2) in mice. We have also observed increased inflammatory cytokines and a type I IFN response following A2 SH N63D infection. We have observed mtDNA release after A2 SH N63D infection within THP-1 cells as well as a STING-dependent type I IFN response Conclusion These results suggest that the aspartic acid within the C-terminus of the SH protein may contribute to RSV pathogenesis and the type I IFN response. Funding Source NIAID R01 AI167249 Topic Categories Viral Immunology (VIR)

analysis_zh.methods: 使用噬菌斑测定、ELISA、胞质 mtDNA 的 qPCR 以及具有 NF-κB 和 I 型 IFN 反应双报告基因的人单核细胞 THP-1 细胞系来研究 N64 突变 的影响。生成 A2 SH N63D 突变体并与野生型 A2 (WT A2) 进行比较。
analysis_zh.main_results: 与野生型 A2 相比,A2 SH N63D 突变体在小鼠体内引起病毒滴度降低和早期疾病。A2 SH N63D 感染后观察到炎症细胞因子增加和 I 型 IFN 反应,以及 THP-1 细胞内 mtDNA 释放和 STING 依赖性 I 型 IFN 反应。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 结果表明,SH 蛋白 C 末端的天冬氨酸可能有助于 RSV 发病机制 和 I 型 IFN 反应。这一发现很新颖,因为它扩展了对 SH 蛋白在 IL-1β 调节之外的作用的理解。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 通过关注 SH 蛋白在 发病机制 中的作用,这些发现可能为针对 RSV 的靶向疗法的开发提供信息。了解 SH 蛋白对疾病严重程度的影响可能会改进 监测 和 RSV 感染的干预策略。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在小鼠和 THP-1 细胞系中进行的,这可能无法完全重现人类 RSV 感染。由于研究范围有限且使用实验室菌株而非临床分离株,证据强度中等。

papers.title: GLUT1 in Memory CD4+ T-cells Correlates with Sustained Antibody Responses and Polyfunctionality Post-RSV Vaccination in Immunocompromised Individuals 2250589
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction The immunogenicity of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccination in immunocompromised individuals is poorly understood due to limited published data in this population, specifically on cellular responses to novel RSV vaccines. To address this gap, T-cell responses were evaluated in immunocompromised individuals who received an approved RSV prefusion F (preF) protein subunit vaccine. Methods In a national prospective observational cohort, 44 immunocompromised individuals reported receiving either adjuvanted RSVPreF3 (AREXVYTM) or unadjuvanted RSVpreF (ABRYSVOTM). The cohort was predominantly solid organ transplant recipients but also included participants with autoimmune conditions on immunosuppressants. T-cell responses, RSV preF antibodies, and RSV neutralizing antibodies were assessed at baseline, early (2 or 4 weeks), and late (12 weeks) post-vaccination using flow cytometry following RSV-A2 fusion protein peptide pool stimulation, ELISA, and live-virus neutralization, respectively. Results Post-vaccination, there were significant increases in RSV-specific memory CD4+ T-cells producing IFN-γ, IL-2, and TNF, and increases in polyfunctional CD4+ T-cells. Both vaccines, without significant differences, increased CD4+ T-cell polyfunctionality. A subset of individuals did not have an increase in CD4+ T-cell responses, demonstrating the need to investigate predictors of response. GLUT1 (Glucose transporter 1) is a marker of T-cell metabolic activation and fitness. In cytokine-producing memory CD4+ T-cells, GLUT1 expression correlated with polyfunctionality, RSV F-specific IgG titers, and neutralizing antibody titers (NT50) at the late but not the early time point. Conclusion These findings suggest that sustained T-cell metabolic fitness, as indicated by GLUT1, may be linked to the durability of both cellular and humoral immune responses. Understanding the role of GLUT1 in shaping immune responses may provide novel methods for optimizing vaccine strategies for immunocompromised individuals. Funding Source National Institutes of Health (NIH) grants 1R01AI190359, 3U01AI138897-04S1, and 3UM1AI109565 Topic Categories Vaccines and Immunotherapy (VAC)

analysis.research_question_and_background: The immunogenicity of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccination in immunocompromised individuals is poorly understood due to limited published data in this population, specifically on cellular responses to novel RSV vaccines.
analysis.study_design_and_population: In a national prospective observational cohort, 44 immunocompromised individuals reported receiving either adjuvanted RSVPreF3 (AREXVYTM) or unadjuvanted RSVpreF (ABRYSVOTM). The cohort was predominantly solid organ transplant recipients but also included participants with autoimmune conditions on immunosuppressants.
analysis.methods: T-cell responses, RSV preF antibodies, and RSV neutralizing antibodies were assessed at baseline, early (2 or 4 weeks), and late (12 weeks) post-vaccination using flow cytometry following RSV-A2 fusion protein peptide pool stimulation, ELISA, and live-virus neutralization, respectively.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the immunogenicity of RSV vaccination in immunocompromised individuals, focusing on T-cell responses and their correlation with antibody durability. In a cohort of 44 immunocompromised participants, both adjuvanted and unadjuvanted RSV vaccines significantly increased polyfunctional CD4+ T-cells and cytokine production. GLUT1 expression in memory CD4+ T-cells correlated with sustained antibody titers and polyfunctionality at 12 weeks post-vaccination, suggesting a role for T-cell metabolic fitness in durable immunity. The findings highlight GLUT1 as a potential biomarker for vaccine response and could guide optimized vaccination strategies for immunocompromised individuals.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 由于该群体中已发表的数据有限,特别是关于新型 RSV 疫苗 的细胞反应的数据有限,因此对 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 疫苗接种 在免疫功能低下个体中的免疫原性知之甚少。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 在一项全国性前瞻性观察 队列研究 中,44 名免疫功能低下者报告接受了有佐剂的 RSVPreF3 (AREXVYTM) 或无佐剂的 RSVpreF (ABRYSVOTM)。队列研究 主要是实体器官移植受者,但也包括因服用免疫抑制剂而患有自身免疫性疾病的参与者。
elements_zh.methods: 在 RSV-A2 融合蛋白肽池刺激、ELISA 和活病毒中和后,分别在基线、疫苗接种 后早期(2 或 4 周)和晚期(12 周)使用流式细胞术评估 T 细胞反应、RSV preF 抗体和 RSV 中和抗体。
elements_zh.main_results: 疫苗接种 后,产生 IFN-γ、IL-2 和 TNF 的 RSV 特异性记忆 CD4+ T 细胞显着增加,并且多功能 CD4+ T 细胞也增加。两种 疫苗 均增加了 CD4+ T 细胞的多功能性,但没有显着差异。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,如 GLUT1 所示,持续的 T 细胞代谢适应性可能与细胞和体液 免疫应答 的持久性有关。了解 GLUT1 在塑造 免疫应答 中的作用可能为优化免疫功能低下个体的 疫苗 策略提供新方法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究将 GLUT1 确定为一种潜在的生物标志物,用于预测免疫功能低下个体 RSV 疫苗接种 后持续抗体反应和多功能 T 细胞反应,这可以为个性化 疫苗 策略提供信息并改善这一弱势群体的结果。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是观察性的,样本量较小,只有 44 名免疫功能低下的个体,这可能会限制普遍性。然而,多重测定和纵向评估的使用为研究结果提供了适度的可信度。

papers.title: Computational Identification of Potential RSV L-RdRp Inhibitors with Predicted Superior Activity and Safety Profiles over Remdesivir Using QSAR Modeling, Molecular Docking and Molecular Dynamics Simulations
papers.abstract: Background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) complex is an essential molecular machine for viral genome replication. The L protein, the catalytic subunit of this complex (L-RdRp), is well-characterized structurally and represents a highly promising target for the development of novel small-molecule drugs against RSV. Methods: To address the limitations of current QSAR-based virtual screening strategies for RSV L-RdRp inhibitor development, we established a multi-dimensional computer-aided drug screening framework integrating activity, toxicity, drug-likeness, and stability. Results: Two OECD-compliant 2D-QSAR models were developed and rigorously validated to predict inhibitory activity and cytotoxicity, respectively. The optimal inhibitory activity model exhibited strong statistical performance, with R2 = 0.8281, QLOO2= 0.7653, Rtest2= 0.8713, QFn2= 0.8594 ∼ 0.8837, CCCtest = 0.9301, MAEtest = 0.1966. Similarly, the best cytotoxicity model achieved R2= 0.8263, QLOO2 = 0.7422, Rtest2 = 0.8951, QFn2 = 0.8108~0.8530, CCCtest = 0.9081, MAEtest = 0.1685. Based on these models, a four-step screening workflow—QSAR-based filtering and molecular docking (15,758 → 2446 → 162 → 19 compounds), ADMET evaluation (19 → 5), and molecular dynamics simulations (MDSs)—was implemented to identify promising L-RdRp inhibitors. Conclusions: Ultimately, five candidate compounds were selected, all of which demonstrated predicted higher inhibitory activity, lower predicted cytotoxicity, a stable predicted binding mode, and favorable oral bioavailability compared with the reference drug remdesivir. These findings provide valuable in silico-derived lead candidates and a reliable computational workflow for identifying experimental L-RdRp inhibitors targeting RSV.

analysis.summary_en: This computational study identified five promising small-molecule inhibitors targeting the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) L-RdRp complex through a multi-dimensional screening framework. The researchers developed rigorously validated 2D-QSAR models to predict inhibitory activity and cytotoxicity, followed by molecular docking, ADMET evaluation, and molecular dynamics simulations. All five selected candidates demonstrated predicted higher inhibitory activity, lower cytotoxicity, stable binding modes, and favorable oral bioavailability compared to remdesivir. While these in silico results provide valuable lead candidates and a reliable computational workflow for RSV drug discovery, experimental validation is needed to confirm their efficacy and safety.

papers.title_zh: 使用 QSAR 建模、分子对接和分子动力学模拟计算鉴定潜在的 RSV L-RdRp 抑制剂,预计其活性和安全性优于瑞德西韦
papers.source_body_en: Background: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp) complex is an essential molecular machine for viral genome replication. The L protein, the catalytic subunit of this complex (L-RdRp), is well-characterized structurally and represents a highly promising target for the development of novel small-molecule drugs against RSV. Methods: To address the limitations of current QSAR-based virtual screening strategies for RSV L-RdRp inhibitor development, we established a multi-dimensional computer-aided drug screening framework integrating activity, toxicity, drug-likeness, and stability. Results: Two OECD-compliant 2D-QSAR models were developed and rigorously validated to predict inhibitory activity and cytotoxicity, respectively. The optimal inhibitory activity model exhibited strong statistical performance, with R2 = 0.8281, QLOO2= 0.7653, Rtest2= 0.8713, QFn2= 0.8594 ∼ 0.8837, CCCtest = 0.9301, MAEtest = 0.1966. Similarly, the best cytotoxicity model achieved R2= 0.8263, QLOO2 = 0.7422, Rtest2 = 0.8951, QFn2 = 0.8108~0.8530, CCCtest = 0.9081, MAEtest = 0.1685. Based on these models, a four-step screening workflow—QSAR-based filtering and molecular docking (15,758 → 2446 → 162 → 19 compounds), ADMET evaluation (19 → 5), and molecular dynamics simulations (MDSs)—was implemented to identify promising L-RdRp inhibitors. Conclusions: Ultimately, five candidate compounds were selected, all of which demonstrated predicted higher inhibitory activity, lower predicted cytotoxicity, a stable predicted binding mode, and favorable oral bioavailability compared with the reference drug remdesivir. These findings provide valuable in silico-derived lead candidates and a reliable computational workflow for identifying experimental L-RdRp inhibitors targeting RSV.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) RNA 依赖性 RNA 聚合酶 (RdRp) 复合物是病毒 基因组 复制的重要分子机器。L 蛋白是该复合物 (L-RdRp) 的催化亚基,其结构特征良好,是开发新型抗 RSV 小分子药物的一个非常有前景的靶点。方法:为了解决当前基于 QSAR 的 RSV L-RdRp 抑制剂开发虚拟筛选策略的局限性,我们建立了一个集活性、毒性、药物相似性和稳定性于一体的多维计算机辅助药物筛选框架。结果:开发了两个符合 OECD 要求的 2D-QSAR 模型并经过严格验证,分别用于预测抑制活性和细胞毒性。最佳抑制活性模型表现出较强的统计性能,R2=0.8281,QLOO2=0.7653,Rtest2=0.8713,QFn2=0.8594∼0.8837,CCCtest=0.9301,MAEtest=0.1966。同样,最佳细胞毒性模型达到R2= 0.8263,QLOO2 = 0.7422,Rtest2 = 0.8951,QFn2 = 0.8108~0.8530,CCCtest = 0.9081,MAEtest = 0.1685。基于这些模型,实施了四步筛选工作流程——基于 QSAR 的过滤和分子对接(15,758 → 2446 → 162 → 19 种化合物)、ADMET 评估(19 → 5)和分子动力学模拟(MDS)——以识别有前景的 L-RdRp 抑制剂。结论:最终筛选出5个候选化合物,与参比药瑞德西韦相比,所有候选化合物均具有较高的抑制活性、较低的细胞毒性、稳定的预测结合模式和良好的口服生物利用度。这些发现为硅衍生的先导候选物提供了有价值的信息,并为识别针对 RSV 的实验性 L-RdRp 抑制剂提供了可靠的计算工作流程。

papers.title: Neuregulin-1 Prevents RSV Induced Disruption of Human Airway Epithelium Polarity 2257854
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Respiratory viruses cause significant morbidity and mortality in very young and old. Mechanism of mortality to respiratory viruses are unknown. We have studied Neuregulin-1 (NRG1), a ligand for ERBb receptor tyrosine kinases (ERBb2 -4) and found pre-treatment with NRG1 provides ∼75% survival for mice infected with normally lethal doses of influenza A or Sendai virus (a rodent para-influenza virus). Administering NRG1 to human bronchial epithelial cells (hBEC) increased epithelial proliferation and repair following infection with RSV. Epithelial barrier function closely links to epithelial polarity; polarized epithelial cells have an apico-basal axis maintained through 3 polarity complexes: PAR (Par3/Par6/aPKC) and CRB (Crumbs/Pals/Patj), apically, and SCRIB (Scrib/Dlg1/Lgl), basolaterally. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) play a role in airway epithelium permeability also affecting polarity. The current study determined the effect of NRG1 on polarity when given prophylactically before RSV infection of hBEC. Methods hBEC grown in transwell were pretreated on the basal side for 5 days with human NRG1 (100 ng) before RSV-gfp (4000 pfu) was added to the apical side. Anti-ERBb2 (10mcg) and anti-ERBb3 (0.1 mcg) antibodies were added for 5 days to the basal side. Immunohistochemistry was performed on paraffin sections for polarity markers (CRB3 and DLG1) d5 post infection. In addition, hBEC were treated for 30 mins at 37oC in CO2 incubator with MitoSOX superoxide indicators to detect mitochondrial superoxide production in live cells. Results NRG1 prevented disruption of CRB3 localization by RSV, an effect blocked by anti-ERBb3. Blocking ERBb2 reduced epithelial proliferation (something ERBb3 antagonism did not do), but did not affect localization of polarity proteins. NRG1 treatment reduced mitoROS in RSV infected cells. Conclusion NRG1 prevents disruption of airway epithelium apico-basal polarity and reduces excessive ROS thus stabilizing hBEC during infection. Funding Source This work was supported by National Institutes of Health (NIH) grants R01AI171027 (to Mitchell H Grayson (MHG)); R01 AI093848 and U19AI42733 (to Mark E Peeples)), the Robert F Wolfe & Edgar T Wolfe Foundation (to MHG). Topic Categories Viral Immunology (VIR)

analysis.research_question_and_background: Respiratory viruses cause significant morbidity and mortality in very young and old, but the mechanisms of mortality are unknown. This study investigated the effect of Neuregulin-1 (NRG1) on maintaining airway epithelium polarity during RSV infection.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used human bronchial epithelial cells (hBEC) grown in transwell pretreated with NRG1 before RSV infection. Cells were treated with anti-ERBb2 and anti-ERBb3 antibodies, and immunohistochemistry was performed for polarity markers.
analysis.methods: hBEC were pretreated with human NRG1 (100 ng) for 5 days before RSV-gfp infection. Immunohistochemistry was performed for CRB3 and DLG1 markers, and mitochondrial superoxide production was detected using MitoSOX indicators.
analysis.main_results: NRG1 prevented disruption of CRB3 localization by RSV, an effect blocked by anti-ERBb3. NRG1 treatment also reduced mitoROS in RSV-infected cells.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that NRG1 stabilizes airway epithelium by preventing disruption of apico-basal polarity and reducing excessive ROS during RSV infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest NRG1 could be a therapeutic candidate to protect airway epithelial integrity during RSV infection, potentially reducing disease severity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was conducted in vitro using hBEC, limiting generalizability to in vivo conditions. The evidence strength is moderate due to the controlled laboratory setting but supported by specific mechanistic findings.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated Neuregulin-1 (NRG1) as a protective agent against RSV-induced disruption of human airway epithelium polarity. Using human bronchial epithelial cells pretreated with NRG1 before RSV infection, the researchers found that NRG1 prevented disruption of CRB3 localization, an effect blocked by anti-ERBb3 antibodies. NRG1 also reduced mitochondrial ROS production in infected cells. The study demonstrates that NRG1 stabilizes airway epithelium by maintaining polarity and reducing oxidative stress during RSV infection, suggesting potential therapeutic applications.

papers.title_zh: Neuregulin-1 防止 RSV 引起的人气道上皮极性破坏 2257854
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Introduction Respiratory viruses cause significant morbidity and mortality in very young and old. Mechanism of mortality to respiratory viruses are unknown. We have studied Neuregulin-1 (NRG1), a ligand for ERBb receptor tyrosine kinases (ERBb2 -4) and found pre-treatment with NRG1 provides ∼75% survival for mice infected with normally lethal doses of influenza A or Sendai virus (a rodent para-influenza virus). Administering NRG1 to human bronchial epithelial cells (hBEC) increased epithelial proliferation and repair following infection with RSV. Epithelial barrier function closely links to epithelial polarity; polarized epithelial cells have an apico-basal axis maintained through 3 polarity complexes: PAR (Par3/Par6/aPKC) and CRB (Crumbs/Pals/Patj), apically, and SCRIB (Scrib/Dlg1/Lgl), basolaterally. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) play a role in airway epithelium permeability also affecting polarity. The current study determined the effect of NRG1 on polarity when given prophylactically before RSV infection of hBEC. Methods hBEC grown in transwell were pretreated on the basal side for 5 days with human NRG1 (100 ng) before RSV-gfp (4000 pfu) was added to the apical side. Anti-ERBb2 (10mcg) and anti-ERBb3 (0.1 mcg) antibodies were added for 5 days to the basal side. Immunohistochemistry was performed on paraffin sections for polarity markers (CRB3 and DLG1) d5 post infection. In addition, hBEC were treated for 30 mins at 37oC in CO2 incubator with MitoSOX superoxide indicators to detect mitochondrial superoxide production in live cells. Results NRG1 prevented disruption of CRB3 localization by RSV, an effect blocked by anti-ERBb3. Blocking ERBb2 reduced epithelial proliferation (something ERBb3 antagonism did not do), but did not affect localization of polarity proteins. NRG1 treatment reduced mitoROS in RSV infected cells. Conclusion NRG1 prevents disruption of airway epithelium apico-basal polarity and reduces excessive ROS thus stabilizing hBEC during infection. Funding Source This work was supported by National Institutes of Health (NIH) grants R01AI171027 (to Mitchell H Grayson (MHG)); R01 AI093848 and U19AI42733 (to Mark E Peeples)), the Robert F Wolfe & Edgar T Wolfe Foundation (to MHG). Topic Categories Viral Immunology (VIR)

papers.title: The role of eosinophils in the management of acute paediatric wheeze: a scoping review
papers.abstract: Acute wheeze is one of the most common paediatric presentations to emergency care. Although blood eosinophils (BEO) are an established biomarker of type 2 inflammation in stable asthma, their role in guiding acute management—particularly systemic corticosteroid use—remains unclear. The aim of this review was to map and synthesise the existing evidence on the measurement and clinical utility of BEO sampled during acute wheeze exacerbations in children. A scoping review was conducted in accordance with Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis extension for scoping reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines. Medline, Embase, Cochrane Library and Web of Science were searched for studies published in the last 20 years involving children under 16 years presenting acutely with wheeze and undergoing eosinophil testing. Prospective and retrospective studies were included. Data were summarised descriptively according to eosinophil measurement methods, reported values, cut-offs and associations with characteristics and treatment response. Eight heterogeneous studies (n = 855) met inclusion criteria, comprising five observational or retrospective studies and three randomised controlled trials. BEO reporting varied widely, with inconsistent units, cut-offs and poorly described sampling timing. No study utilised point-of-care testing. Across studies, eosinophil dynamics differed by age, wheeze phenotype, disease severity and viral aetiology, preventing meaningful comparison. Evidence supporting eosinophil-guided corticosteroid use was limited. Two studies demonstrated improved outcomes with systemic corticosteroids in children with rhinovirus-associated wheeze and higher BEO, while lower BEO were observed in respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-associated wheeze. There is a paucity of high-quality data describing BEO during acute wheeze exacerbations in children. Current evidence underpinning eosinophil-guided care is largely derived from stable outpatient cohorts and may not be directly applicable to acute settings. Prospective studies with standardised sampling of BEO during acute presentations are needed to inform precision-based corticosteroid use.

papers.title_zh: 嗜酸性粒细胞在小儿急性喘息治疗中的作用:范围审查
papers.source_body_en: Acute wheeze is one of the most common paediatric presentations to emergency care. Although blood eosinophils (BEO) are an established biomarker of type 2 inflammation in stable asthma, their role in guiding acute management—particularly systemic corticosteroid use—remains unclear. The aim of this review was to map and synthesise the existing evidence on the measurement and clinical utility of BEO sampled during acute wheeze exacerbations in children. A scoping review was conducted in accordance with Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis extension for scoping reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guidelines. Medline, Embase, Cochrane Library and Web of Science were searched for studies published in the last 20 years involving children under 16 years presenting acutely with wheeze and undergoing eosinophil testing. Prospective and retrospective studies were included. Data were summarised descriptively according to eosinophil measurement methods, reported values, cut-offs and associations with characteristics and treatment response. Eight heterogeneous studies (n = 855) met inclusion criteria, comprising five observational or retrospective studies and three randomised controlled trials. BEO reporting varied widely, with inconsistent units, cut-offs and poorly described sampling timing. No study utilised point-of-care testing. Across studies, eosinophil dynamics differed by age, wheeze phenotype, disease severity and viral aetiology, preventing meaningful comparison. Evidence supporting eosinophil-guided corticosteroid use was limited. Two studies demonstrated improved outcomes with systemic corticosteroids in children with rhinovirus-associated wheeze and higher BEO, while lower BEO were observed in respiratory syncytial virus (RSV)-associated wheeze. There is a paucity of high-quality data describing BEO during acute wheeze exacerbations in children. Current evidence underpinning eosinophil-guided care is largely derived from stable outpatient cohorts and may not be directly applicable to acute settings. Prospective studies with standardised sampling of BEO during acute presentations are needed to inform precision-based corticosteroid use.

papers.title: Equity-by-design in RSV immunisation development
papers.abstract: Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infects nearly all children by age two, with reinfections common throughout life. While most infections cause mild upper respiratory symptoms, RSV can cause severe, potentially fatal lower respiratory tract infections in infants, particularly premature babies and those with comorbidities, with outcomes often worse in low- and lower-middle-income countries (LMICs) lacking adequate healthcare access. Until recently, palivizumab (a short-acting monoclonal antibody, mAb) was the only approved preventive option, but its high cost limited use to high-risk infants. Nirsevimab (2022) became the first long-acting mAb approved for all infants, followed by a maternal RSV vaccine, and clesrovimab (2025). The WHO now recommends RSV prevention via maternal vaccination or mAbs, but LMIC implementation lags due to logistical and financial barriers and gaps in safety and efficacy data. This thesis uses five research types across the translational spectrum to address inequities in infant RSV immunization access in LMICs: public health, basic, preclinical, clinical, and implementation research. Key Findings: Chapter 2 reviews the RSV vaccine/mAb landscape (as of June 2024: 5 marketed products, 30 in development), noting nirsevimab's >80% effectiveness against RSV hospitalization, while access remains concentrated in high-income countries despite LMICs bearing the greatest disease burden. Chapter 3 argues that access-to-medicine mechanisms (voluntary licensing, technology transfer) combined with WHO prequalification and funding mechanisms like Gavi are essential for affordable LMIC access. Chapter 4 identifies barriers and facilitators for maternal immunization in Soweto, South Africa, through co-creation workshops with healthcare workers, yielding recommendations on education, community awareness, reporting incentives, and improved medical record-keeping. Chapters 5–7 describe developing and validating a dried blood RSV-neutralizing antibody assay (using samples from a Gates MRI RSM01 phase 1 trial), showing dried blood can replace serum in bioanalyses (R2 > 0.95), and successfully transferring this assay to a Ghanaian laboratory, strengthening local research capacity. Chapters 8–9 cover industry-independent development of intranasal palivizumab drops. A phase 2b RCT in late-preterm infants found daily intranasal dosing was safe but did not significantly prevent RSV infection (38.3% vs 23.4% placebo). A controlled human infection model study in adults showed no reduction in viral titer despite a 72% reduction in symptomatic infections, suggesting intranasal mAbs are unlikely to be a viable, cost-effective protection strategy. Chapter 10 evaluates mAb-resistant mutants (MARMs) under suboptimal antibody pressure for palivizumab, nirsevimab, and RSM01, finding RSM01 has a higher resistance barrier and that resistance generally reduces viral fitness, making global dominance of resistant strains unlikely. Discussion The thesis argues that current RSV product development follows a "trickle-down" approach designed for high-income contexts. It proposes an equity-by-design framework built on three lessons (begin with the end in mind, simplify methods for LMIC contexts, embed affordability early) and four recommendations: scientific co-ownership with LMIC partners, operational investment in local capacity, economic feasibility built in from early development, and social integration with community priorities—positioning equity as a foundational principle rather than an afterthought in RSV immunization development.

A phase 2b RCT in late-preterm infants found daily intranasal dosing was safe but did not significantly prevent RSV infection (38.3% vs 23.4% placebo). A controlled human infection model study in adults showed no reduction in viral titer despite a 72% reduction in symptomatic infections, suggesting intranasal mAbs are unlikely to be a viable, cost-effective protection strategy. It proposes an equity-by-design framework built on three lessons (begin with the end in mind, simplify methods for LMIC contexts, embed affordability early) and four recommendations: scientific co-ownership with LMIC partners, operational investment in local capacity, economic feasibility built in from early development, and social integration with community priorities—positioning equity as a foundational principle rather than an afterthought in RSV immunization development.

Key Findings: Chapter 2 reviews the RSV vaccine/mAb landscape (as of June 2024: 5 marketed products, 30 in development), noting nirsevimab's >80% effectiveness against RSV hospitalization, while access remains concentrated in high-income countries despite LMICs bearing the greatest disease burden. papers.title: Versatile Subwavelength Grating Microring Resonators for Label-Free and Multiplex-Compatible Detection of Respiratory Viruses
papers.abstract: Abstract Respiratory viruses, such as the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), influenza A (H1N1), and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), remain major public health threats due to overlapping clinical symptoms and the limited speed, sensitivity, and multiplexing capacity of conventional diagnostic methods. Here, we present a label-free optical biosensing platform based on subwavelength grating microring resonators (SGMRRs) for the sensitive and specific detection of viral antigens. The sensor surface is functionalized with antibodies against three representative viral proteins, enabling quantitative detection via resonance wavelength shifts upon antigen binding. The platform achieves the refractive index limit of detection (LoD) of 1.25×10−4 RIU and enables the detection of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein at 100 pg/mL, the H1N1 nucleoprotein at 10 pg/mL, and the RSV F-trimer protein at 10 pg/mL. The compact SGMRR design readily supports multiplexed integration through multi-ring or multi-channel architectures, highlighting its potential as a scalable and high-performance platform for rapid, quantitative, and point-of-care viral diagnostics.

papers.source_body_en: Abstract Respiratory viruses, such as the severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), influenza A (H1N1), and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), remain major public health threats due to overlapping clinical symptoms and the limited speed, sensitivity, and multiplexing capacity of conventional diagnostic methods. Here, we present a label-free optical biosensing platform based on subwavelength grating microring resonators (SGMRRs) for the sensitive and specific detection of viral antigens. The sensor surface is functionalized with antibodies against three representative viral proteins, enabling quantitative detection via resonance wavelength shifts upon antigen binding. The platform achieves the refractive index limit of detection (LoD) of 1.25×10−4 RIU and enables the detection of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein at 100 pg/mL, the H1N1 nucleoprotein at 10 pg/mL, and the RSV F-trimer protein at 10 pg/mL. The compact SGMRR design readily supports multiplexed integration through multi-ring or multi-channel architectures, highlighting its potential as a scalable and high-performance platform for rapid, quantitative, and point-of-care viral diagnostics.

papers.title: Immune Dysregulation in Down Syndrome: Implications for Infectious Susceptibility and Vaccine Response
papers.abstract: Down syndrome (DS), caused by trisomy 21, is characterized by complex immune dysregulation that increases susceptibility to infections and alters vaccine responsiveness. Gene dosage effects involving interferon receptor loci on chromosome 21 contribute to chronic type I interferon hyperactivation, sustained JAK-STAT signaling, and persistent expression of interferon-stimulated genes. This baseline inflammatory state is accompanied by quantitative and functional defects in both innate and adaptive immunity, including impaired neutrophil chemotaxis, pro-inflammatory monocyte polarization, reduced naïve T- and B-cell compartments, restricted antigen receptor diversity, diminished class-switched memory B cells, and features of accelerated immunosenescence. Clinically, these immune alterations are associated with an increased risk of severe respiratory viral infections, such as respiratory syncytial virus, influenza, and SARS-CoV-2, as well as reduced magnitude and durability of vaccine-induced immunity. Cohort studies in both pediatric and adult populations have reported higher rates of hospitalization and mortality, along with lower peak antibody titers and more rapid waning of immunity following vaccination. This review integrates molecular, cellular, and clinical evidence to define the interferon-driven immune phenotype in DS and its implications for susceptibility to infection and vaccination response. A mechanistic understanding of this immune landscape provides a framework for developing tailored preventive strategies and optimizing vaccination approaches in this vulnerable population.

papers.abstract_zh: 唐氏综合症 (DS) 由 21 三体引起,其特征是复杂的免疫失调,增加对感染的易感性并改变 疫苗 反应性。涉及 21 号染色体上干扰素受体基因座的基因剂量效应有助于慢性 I 型干扰素过度激活、持续的 JAK-STAT 信号传导以及干扰素刺激基因的持续表达。这种基线炎症状态伴随着先天性和适应性免疫的数量和功能缺陷,包括中性粒细胞趋化性受损、促炎性单核细胞极化、幼稚T细胞和B细胞区室减少、抗原受体多样性受限、类别转换记忆B细胞减少以及加速免疫衰老的特征。临床上,这些免疫改变与严重呼吸道病毒感染(例如 呼吸道合胞病毒、流感和 SARS-CoV-2)的风险增加以及 疫苗 诱导的免疫力的强度和持久性降低有关。队列研究 在儿童和成人人群中的研究报告了 队列研究 后住院率和 死亡率 较高,以及 疫苗接种 后峰值抗体滴度较低和免疫力更快减弱。本综述整合了分子、细胞和临床证据来定义 DS 中干扰素驱动的免疫表型及其对感染易感性和 疫苗接种 反应的影响。对这种免疫环境的机械理解为针对这一弱势群体制定量身定制的预防策略和优化 疫苗接种 方法提供了一个框架。

papers.title: Epidemiology of viral and atypical bacterial respiratory infections among children hospitalised at a Kenyan tertiary referral centre: a cross sectional multiplex PCR study
papers.abstract: Background Severe acute respiratory infections (SARIs) cause high paediatric morbidity and mortality particularly in sub-Saharan Africa. Understanding contemporary trends in SARI aetiology is needed to inform prevention strategies. We aimed to determine the current aetiology, severity and seasonality of SARIs based on pathogens detected by multiplex quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) tests, BioFire® respiratory panel 2.0 (RP 2) and 2.1 plus (RP2.1 plus ) Methods We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional analytic study among Kenyan children aged 0–18 years hospitalised between March 2018 and March 2023, with SARI and a positive nasopharyngeal swab multiplex qRT-PCR test. Cases were analyzed for their clinical characteristics, radiological features, laboratory data, seasonality of the respiratory pathogens and risk factors for severe infection. Results A total of 545 pathogens were detected in 382 cases,123 (22.5%) had polymicrobial detection, 14 (4%) had severe illness and three (0.8%) died. Rhinovirus (24%) and respiratory syncytial virus (21%) were the most common viral pathogens identified whereas Mycoplasma pneumoniae (2.4%) and Bordetella pertussis (1.8%) were the most common atypical pathogens detected. Infections peaked during the first dry season and the short rainy season. Lower respiratory tract infections and presence of co-morbidities like asthma,vitamin D deficiency and iron deficiency anaemia were associated with disease severity independent of age, sex and seasonality. Conclusions Viruses accounted for majority of respiratory infections. Infections had two distinct peaks: the first dry season and the short rainy season, suggesting that respiratory vaccines should be scheduled prior to their onset.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Severe acute respiratory infections (SARIs) impose substantial paediatric morbidity and mortality in sub-Saharan Africa, and contemporary aetiological data are needed to guide prevention strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cross-sectional analytic study was conducted among Kenyan children aged 0–18 years hospitalised with SARI and a positive nasopharyngeal swab multiplex qRT-PCR test between March 2018 and March 2023.
analysis.methods: Multiplex quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) tests, BioFire® respiratory panel 2.0 (RP 2) and 2.1 plus (RP2.1 plus), were used to detect pathogens; cases were analyzed for clinical characteristics, radiological features, laboratory data, seasonality and risk factors for severe infection.
analysis.main_results: A total of 545 pathogens were detected in 382 cases, with 123 (22.5%) polymicrobial detections, 14 (4%) severe illnesses and three (0.8%) deaths; rhinovirus (24%) and respiratory syncytial virus (21%) were the most common viral pathogens.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Viruses accounted for the majority of respiratory infections, and infections peaked during the first dry season and the short rainy season, suggesting seasonality-driven scheduling of respiratory vaccines.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings indicate that RSV contributes substantially to paediatric SARI hospitalisations in Kenya and that vaccine timing should align with seasonal peaks to maximise impact.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s retrospective design and reliance on multiplex PCR without confirmatory viral culture limit causal inference and may underestimate co-infections, warranting moderate confidence in the evidence.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective cross-sectional study in Kenyan children hospitalised with SARI used multiplex qRT-PCR to identify respiratory pathogens between 2018 and 2023. Among 382 cases, 545 pathogens were detected, with RSV identified in 21% of infections, second only to rhinovirus. Viral aetiology predominated, and infections peaked during the first dry season and short rainy season. Lower respiratory tract involvement and comorbidities such as asthma and vitamin D deficiency were associated with severe disease. The authors conclude that RSV is a major contributor to paediatric SARI and recommend aligning vaccination schedules with seasonal peaks to reduce burden.

elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 病毒占呼吸道感染的大部分,感染在第一个旱季和短暂的雨季达到高峰,这表明呼吸道 疫苗 的调度是季节性驱动的。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,RSV 对肯尼亚儿科 SARI 住院造成了重大影响,疫苗 的时间应与季节性高峰保持一致,以最大限度地发挥影响。

papers.title: Development of a nomogram for risk factors of wheezing in infants with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia
papers.abstract: To construct a nomogram model for analyzing risk factors of wheezing in infants with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (MPP), so as to provide evidence for clinical intervention. A retrospective analysis was performed on clinical data of 569 infants with MPP hospitalized in the Department of Respiratory Medicine and Department of Infectious Diseases, Children’s Hospital of Soochow University. They were divided into a wheezing group (204 cases) and a non-wheezing group (365 cases) according to symptoms. Demographic characteristics, clinical manifestations, laboratory examinations, bronchoscopy frequency and chest imaging findings were collected. Differences in clinical and laboratory indicators between the two groups were compared. Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression was used for preliminary screening, followed by Logistic regression to identify independent risk factors for wheezing in infants with MPP. Finally, a nomogram prediction model was established, and its performance was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve and decision curve analysis (DCA). Univariate and multivariate analysis of predictors for wheezing in MPP: Univariate Logistic regression screening revealed 16 potential risk factors: fever, cough, history of wheezing, history of eczema, WBC, N#, L#, PLT, CRP, IgG, IgM, CKMB, D-D (ug/L), HRV, HRSV, HMPV ( P < 0.05). Multivariate Logistic regression showed that history of wheezing (OR = 5.894, 95%CI: 3.541–9.812), history of eczema (OR = 1.951, 95%CI: 1.295–2.939), elevated IgG (OR = 1.166, 95%CI: 1.074–1.266), elevated CKMB (OR = 1.083, 95%CI: 1.007–1.164), and combined HRSV infection (OR = 3.430, 95%CI: 1.819–6.468) were risk factors, while fever (OR = 0.389, 95%CI: 0.252–0.599) was a protective factor against wheezing in infants with MPP. Establishment and validation of the nomogram model: Based on multivariate Logistic regression, six indicators were included to construct the nomogram for predicting wheezing in MPP: history of wheezing, history of eczema, elevated IgG, elevated CKMB, combined HRSV infection, and fever. Each predictor was scored independently, and the total score corresponded to the predicted probability of wheezing caused by MPP. Model evaluation: Training set: AUC = 0.7862, sensitivity = 72.4%, specificity = 78.1%; Internal validation set: AUC = 0.6863, sensitivity = 53.7%, specificity = 79.5%, indicating favorable discrimination. DCA suggested potential clinical applicability.To further evaluate the robustness of the nomogram and to correct for potential optimism, we performed 200 bootstrap resampling iterations within the development cohort. The optimism-corrected area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was calculated by subtracting the average optimism (estimated from the difference between apparent performance in each bootstrap sample and the performance applied to the original dataset) from the training-set AUC. The corrected AUC was 0.705 (95% CI: 0.662–0.748), which is consistent with the internal validation result (AUC = 0.686) and indicates moderate discriminative ability. Although the corrected AUC remained above 0.70, the decline from the training-set AUC (0.786) suggests some degree of overfitting, likely attributable to the single-center retrospective design and limited sample size. These bootstrap-corrected estimates support the potential clinical utility of the nomogram. Atopic constitution and mixed viral infection are risk factors for wheezing in infants with MPP. The nomogram model is clinically valuable for predicting wheezing in infants with MPP.

The corrected AUC was 0.705 (95% CI: 0.662–0.748), which is consistent with the internal validation result (AUC = 0.686) and indicates moderate discriminative ability. Although the corrected AUC remained above 0.70, the decline from the training-set AUC (0.786) suggests some degree of overfitting, likely attributable to the single-center retrospective design and limited sample size. These bootstrap-corrected estimates support the potential clinical utility of the nomogram. Atopic constitution and mixed viral infection are risk factors for wheezing in infants with MPP. The nomogram model is clinically valuable for predicting wheezing in infants with MPP.

papers.source_body_en: To construct a nomogram model for analyzing risk factors of wheezing in infants with Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (MPP), so as to provide evidence for clinical intervention. A retrospective analysis was performed on clinical data of 569 infants with MPP hospitalized in the Department of Respiratory Medicine and Department of Infectious Diseases, Children’s Hospital of Soochow University. They were divided into a wheezing group (204 cases) and a non-wheezing group (365 cases) according to symptoms. Demographic characteristics, clinical manifestations, laboratory examinations, bronchoscopy frequency and chest imaging findings were collected. Differences in clinical and laboratory indicators between the two groups were compared. Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression was used for preliminary screening, followed by Logistic regression to identify independent risk factors for wheezing in infants with MPP. Finally, a nomogram prediction model was established, and its performance was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve and decision curve analysis (DCA). Univariate and multivariate analysis of predictors for wheezing in MPP: Univariate Logistic regression screening revealed 16 potential risk factors: fever, cough, history of wheezing, history of eczema, WBC, N#, L#, PLT, CRP, IgG, IgM, CKMB, D-D (ug/L), HRV, HRSV, HMPV ( P < 0.05). Multivariate Logistic regression showed that history of wheezing (OR = 5.894, 95%CI: 3.541–9.812), history of eczema (OR = 1.951, 95%CI: 1.295–2.939), elevated IgG (OR = 1.166, 95%CI: 1.074–1.266), elevated CKMB (OR = 1.083, 95%CI: 1.007–1.164), and combined HRSV infection (OR = 3.430, 95%CI: 1.819–6.468) were risk factors, while fever (OR = 0.389, 95%CI: 0.252–0.599) was a protective factor against wheezing in infants with MPP. Establishment and validation of the nomogram model: Based on multivariate Logistic regression, six indicators were included to construct the nomogram for predicting wheezing in MPP: history of wheezing, history of eczema, elevated IgG, elevated CKMB, combined HRSV infection, and fever. Each predictor was scored independently, and the total score corresponded to the predicted probability of wheezing caused by MPP. Model evaluation: Training set: AUC = 0.7862, sensitivity = 72.4%, specificity = 78.1%; Internal validation set: AUC = 0.6863, sensitivity = 53.7%, specificity = 79.5%, indicating favorable discrimination. DCA suggested potential clinical applicability.To further evaluate the robustness of the nomogram and to correct for potential optimism, we performed 200 bootstrap resampling iterations within the development cohort. The optimism-corrected area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) was calculated by subtracting the average optimism (estimated from the difference between apparent performance in each bootstrap sample and the performance applied to the original dataset) from the training-set AUC. The corrected AUC was 0.705 (95% CI: 0.662–0.748), which is consistent with the internal validation result (AUC = 0.686) and indicates moderate discriminative ability. Although the corrected AUC remained above 0.70, the decline from the training-set AUC (0.786) suggests some degree of overfitting, likely attributable to the single-center retrospective design and limited sample size. These bootstrap-corrected estimates support the potential clinical utility of the nomogram. Atopic constitution and mixed viral infection are risk factors for wheezing in infants with MPP. The nomogram model is clinically valuable for predicting wheezing in infants with MPP.

This page presents a snapshot of current acute respiratory infection activity in Tasmania. Current activity is presented for acute respiratory illness and specific notifiable viruses, these are COVID-19, influenza, and RSV. Acute respiratory illness is an overall indicator and may be due to symptoms of various infections including COVID-19, influenza, RSV, Rhinovirus and others. Activity may be presented as low, moderate or high. While monitoring by Public Health Services is continuous, this page is updated monthly during inter-seasonal periods. During increased seasonal influenza and RSV activity, this page is updated fortnightly.For detailed respiratory surveillance see RespTas report.Understanding current activity of acute respiratory infections will help you stay informed, follow activity level link to learn more about what steps you can take to reduce the risk to yourselves and others. analysis.brief_en: The Tasmanian Department of Health has issued an update on acute respiratory infection activity as of 19 July 2026. While overall acute respiratory illness (ARI) activity remains low but is gradually increasing, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) stands out with moderate and increasing activity, consistent with seasonal patterns. The department updates this information fortnightly during heightened seasonal periods and directs the public to the RespTas report for detailed surveillance data. Authorities emphasize that understanding current activity levels helps individuals take informed steps to reduce transmission risks.

news.source_body_en: The Tasmanian Department of Health has issued an update on acute respiratory infection activity as of 19 July 2026. While overall acute respiratory illness (ARI) activity remains low but is gradually increasing, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) stands out with moderate and increasing activity, consistent with seasonal patterns. In contrast, COVID-19 and influenza activity remain low, with influenza below expected levels compared to recent years. The department updates this information fortnightly during heightened seasonal periods and directs the public to the RespTas report for detailed surveillance data. Authorities emphasize that understanding current activity levels helps individuals take informed steps to reduce transmission risks.
news.content_zh: 塔斯马尼亚卫生部发布了截至 2026 年 7 月 19 日急性呼吸道感染活动的最新信息。虽然总体急性呼吸道疾病 (ARI) 活动仍然较低,但正在逐渐增加,但 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 的活动中度且有所增加,与季节性模式一致。相比之下,COVID-19 和流感活动仍然较低,与近年来相比,流感水平低于预期水平。该部门在旺季期间每两周更新一次此信息,并引导公众查看 RespTas 报告以获取详细的 监测 数据。当局强调,了解当前的活动水平有助于个人采取明智的措施来降低 传播 风险。
